phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎬᏱ ᎨᎲ ᎬᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᏰᎸᏛ ᏥᏂᎾᏛᏁᎠ ᏣᎾᏔᏅ ᏓᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎠᎭᎾ

phrases.english_text: First let me tell you the reason we are doing this. You know that kids are going to school here?

phrases.phonetic_broad: vv

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏢᏴ ᏛᎾᎴᏂ ᎠᎾᏛᏓᏍᏗᎲ Ꭿ ᏥᏂᏬᏂ ᏓᏂᏬᏂᏏ Ꮥ
phrases.phonetic_text: skitv lhvy tvnleni anthvtahstihv hi tsiniwoni taniwonihs te
phrases.phonetic_broad: skitv lvy tvnleni antvtastiv i tsiniwoni taniwonis te
phrases.english_text: One of these days they are going to start listening to us, talking how we are. Or we are going to be talking, [for them] to listen to how Cherokee is spoken. I don’t know if they are going to get that far—but the reason is for them to listen. And, also, your grandchildren or your immediate family might want to someday listen to you talking. If they come here and ask, they will let them listen to you talking, or us talking. As we begin, tell me your full name in English.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮩ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏝᏅ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏍᎩ Ᏼ ᏳᏛᏅᏟᎶᏝ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᎤᏰᎵᏗ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ ᏐᎢᏂ ᎨᎲ

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏦᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏓᎵ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏝ ᏅᏱ ᎣᏓᎳ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏝ Jackson Mountain ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏝ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ ᏣᎾᏛ Ꮎ Mankiller flats ᏣᏃᏎᎰ

phrases.english_text: We just made things to play with. And just down the hill there was a big creek where we had a place to swim. We would clean it out.

phrases.phonetic_text: v'v

phrases.english_text: Really. That stomp ground has been there a long time.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏕᏂ ᏣᎳᏂᏥᏟᏍᎪ ᏣᏕᏅ ᏂᎯᏍᎪ ᎦᏳᎵᏍᎪ

phrases.english_text: When you were born, when [you] came into [life], when you were born, was it already there?

phrases.phonetic_text: kayli tv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kayli tv
phrases.english_text: It already was.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏙᏓ Ꮫ ᎤᏂᎩᏍᏗᏗᏎ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ

phrases.english_text: Your dad was keeping it running back then.

phrases.phonetic_text: etot tsikhv tsunikhsttihsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: etot tsikv tsuniksttisv
phrases.english_text: My dad kept it running.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎾ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏃᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎦᎵᏍᏔᏅ Ꮩ ᎮᎵ ᏓᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂ

phrases.phonetic_text: heli k khilo ta'ayvhstvni
phrases.phonetic_broad: eli k kilo taayvstvni
phrases.english_text: What if someday something happens? What do you think is going to happen to it? Do you think someone will take over?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏔᎵᏛ ᎠᏁᏙᎰ ᏧᏂᏓᎨ ᎠᏂᏧᏥ ᎤᎾᏚᎵ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎮ ᏙᎦᏥᏲᎯᏐᏁᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: anithaltv antoho tsunitake anitstsi untuli skwu ahe tktsiyohihsonheli
phrases.phonetic_broad: anitaltv antoo tsunitake anitstsi untuli skwu ae tktsiyoisoneli
phrases.english_text: Two young boys, that go there, want to. I guess I am going to hand it over to them.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎪᏍ ᎢᏣᏗᏍᎪ ᏙᎨ ᎢᏦᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᎾᏕᏲᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: n taninhokihskohs itsatihsko tokhe itsohe skina tsanhateyho
phrases.phonetic_broad: n taninokiskos itsatisko toke itsoe skina tsanateyo
phrases.english_text: Do they sing? You all say, or what do you call that, when they go around?

phrases.phonetic_text: taninhokihsko tv antiho
phrases.phonetic_broad: taninokisko tv antio
phrases.english_text: They say they sing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏂ ᎠᎭ ᎠᏂᏰᎵᎰ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ

phrases.phonetic_broad: nani aa aniyelio tsanatio to ust nusti skna

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎩ ᎠᏰᎵᏙᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: skina akvyi anikihski ayhelitoho
phrases.phonetic_broad: skina akvyi anikiski ayelitoo

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᎠᏂᏐᏅ ᎠᎾᏓᏍᏓᏩᏕᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: o anihsonv antahstawatekho
phrases.phonetic_broad: o anisonv antastawateko
phrases.english_text: So, the others follow?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᎾᏓᏍᏓᏩᏕᎪ ᏃᏭ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᏏᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᏔᎵᏁ ᏣᏂ ᏓᎦᏏ ᏧᎾᏅᏒᏛᏍᎩ ᏃᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: antahstawteko nhowu uneln sin na anikeyha thalin tsani takhs tsnnvhsthsk nowu
phrases.phonetic_broad: antastawteko nowu uneln sin na anikeya talin tsani taks tsnnvstsk nowu
phrases.english_text: The others just follow them. And there are other women that dance, that wear the turtle shells.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏍᎪ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾᏛᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihsko ika anehi skhi nntvne
phrases.phonetic_broad: elisko ika anei ski nntvne
phrases.english_text: Are there quite a few of them?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵ ᎣᏏ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏏᏛ ᎠᎾᏕᎳᏆ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎩ ᏍᏊ ᏩᏂ ᎠᏁᏙᎰ ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎲ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: eli ohsi ika anehi sitv anatlkwa nle aniyoneki skwu wani anetoho untulihv unatelkwahsti ski nuhstv
phrases.phonetic_broad: eli osi ika anei sitv anatlkwa nle aniyoneki skwu wani anetoo untuliv unatelkwasti ski nustv
phrases.english_text: There are quite a few, and some are still learning. And also, White people come over there, wanting to learn things like that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏕᏣᎵᏍᎪᎵᏓᏁᎰᏍ ᎤᎾᎵᏍᎩᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: tetsalhskoltanehohs unlhskihsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: tetsalskoltaneos unlskisti
phrases.english_text: And you all let them dance?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏧᎾᏁᎵᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: nle skwalhehsti ika tsnn'elhihti
phrases.phonetic_broad: nle skwalesti ika tsnneliti
phrases.english_text: And play ball on game day.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis
phrases.english_text: Is there --

phrases.english_text: That is the reason, I think, for whatever kind of person that comes—that wants to learn.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏅ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᎢᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏛᏲᏲᎱᏎᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinv nkehvni iki ika tyo'yohuhseli

phrases.english_text: If not for that, you'll lose it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏛᏲᏲᎱᏎᎵ Ꮫ
phrases.phonetic_text: tyyohuhsel tv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tyyousel tv
phrases.english_text: You'll lose it.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏣᎾᎳᏍᎦᎵᏍᎪ ᎡᎵᏍ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᎳᏍᎦᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: n tsanlahskalihsko elihs skahsti anlahskali
phrases.phonetic_broad: n tsanlaskalisko elis skasti anlaskali

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮭ ᎤᏟ Ꭱ ᎤᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏱᎾᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ Ᏺ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏴ ᏱᏍᏓᏯ ᏗᏁᏟᏗ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: lha utli e uhskahsti ynnatnho ytaha yo ahsen tlha skiy yihstay tinelhihti ik katsiyhsho
phrases.phonetic_broad: la utli e uskasti ynnatno ytaa yo asen tla skiy yistay tineliti ik katsiyso
phrases.english_text: Not really, they can get rough sometimes. But I tell them, you don’t have to play that hard.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏚ Ꮂ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohstu hv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ostu v
phrases.english_text: Just normal.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏚ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏃᏰᏂᏭ ᏓᏅᏗᎰ ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ ᏃᏭ ᏗᎳᏍᎦᎵᏙᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohstu anikey hen tsnoyeniw tanvhtiho anihskay now tilahsklitoti
phrases.phonetic_broad: ostu anikey en tsnoyeniw tanvtio aniskay now tilasklitoti

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏬᏢᏗᎭ Ꮫ ᏓᎾᏁᎶᎲᏍᎪ ᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗ ᏓᏂᎦᎳᏫᏐ ᏍᎩᎾ

phrases.english_text: Just normal. The women use their hands, and the men use ball sticks. They play ball, all in fun, and joke around.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏳᏁᎵᏌᏭᏍ ᏳᏭᏂᏑᎵᎪᏍᏗ ᏙᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: yunelihswhs ywunihsulikohsti tokhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: yunelisws ywunisulikosti toke

phrases.syllabary_text: yeah ᏳᏁᎵᏐᏭ ᏳᏂᏑᎵᎪᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎨᏛ Ꮎ ᎾᏭ ᎠᏥᎳ ᏗᎲ ᏯᏂᏍᏛᏅᏅᎩ

phrases.phonetic_broad: ya yunelisowu ynisliksti na eni aan ketv n nawu atsila tiv yanistnvnvk
phrases.english_text: Yes, just when they decide when to stop. Where the pole is, here, and where the fire is, they will draw a line. We have a ball up there this big [gestures] and when they hit that they count it four—it if it hits below that, it’s one. They draw lines there for --

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗᏅ ᎣᎩᏢᏅ Ꭿ ᏱᎩᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏅᏂᎳ ᏅᎩ ᏓᏅᏎᏍᏗᎰ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏗᏝ ᏳᏩᏂᎵ ᏌᏭ ᎤᎾ ᏓᏂᏍᏛᏅᏅᏍᎪ

phrases.english_text: Yes, just when they decide when to stop. Where the pole is, here, and where the fire is, they will draw a line. We have a ball up there this big [gestures] and when they hit that they count it four—it if it hits below that, it’s one. They draw lines there for --

phrases.phonetic_text: unina'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: uninav
phrases.english_text: -- What their score is?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᎴ ᏱᏗᎤᎾᎦᏛᎲᏏ ᏥᎤᏂᎷᏥ ᎤᎾᏓᏠᏒ ᎨᎰ

phrases.phonetic_broad: nole ytiunakatvs tsiunilutsi unattlosv keo
phrases.english_text: Yes, and when they turn around and come back, they have won.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏓᏍᏓᏅᎾ Ꮥ
phrases.phonetic_text: tahstnvnha te
phrases.phonetic_broad: tastnvna te

phrases.phonetic_text: ya tnihstvhnnvhsko
phrases.phonetic_broad: ya tnistvnnvsko
phrases.english_text: Yes, there are lines, where they draw lines.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎮᏍᏕ ᏯᏩᏅᏖ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏂᏅᏍᎬ ᎾᎮᏂ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏕᏥᎦᏘ

phrases.english_text: I didn’t know what they did to score, over at Belfonte, where I pastor. There’s a group of young people, they go around playing ball. They went and played at Fayetteville, and I went and watched them. They also said this next month in Fort Smith there is going to be a big tournament and they are going, they said. They said there are 25 teams, I think, are involved. They were saying. They said a lot of them are from Mississippi. Boy they are going to have a rough ballgame.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛ Ꮎ ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏱᎾᏅᏛᎩ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏙᎭ

phrases.syllabary_text: ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏱᎾᎾᏛᎦ ᎮᏍᏗᎡ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏲᎨᏙᎶ ᎠᏴ

phrases.phonetic_text: lhahsyo
phrases.phonetic_broad: lasyo
phrases.english_text: You don’t?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᏴᏓᎭ Ꮓ ᎠᏂᏧᏥ ᎠᎾᏖᎳᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏳᏂᏍᏆᎸᎡᎵ Ꮎ Cherokee holiday Ꮎ man to man ᎨᎵ ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎠᎾᏖᎳᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏂᏧᏥ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v ytaha no antshutsi anathelatihsko ahan yunihskwal'el n tsawakhi hawate na man tu man keli tstanheho ikati antheltihsko anitsuhtsi

phrases.english_text: They pay them more than they do the other workers. I was the leader of 12 when I retired. We were out there in the field with the bosses. I said to him. “Some different people are going to come. I think 30 of them. phrases.english_text: One time at Rocky Mountain, to the south, my grandfather lived on a hill. Me and the boys were walking in the field. And they said “There is a big hole over there in the ground.” We went there, and there was a locust [tree] this big [gestures]. It was long and sticking in there—it was just smooth. I don’t know if it was coons or something was crawling around on there, it was clean. It was just smooth. “Y’all get away,,” the boy said. “Let’s leave!”, he said. We went across to where Wilma Mankiller lives. We used to live there a long time ago. We used to cross straight through there to where my grandfather lived. We went just a little ways, and an old lady screamed. She said, “Hey where did you boys go? You all come back,” she said.

phrases.english_text: Yeah. When that bean picker [truck] started coming, it was coming just right. The pickers are this big [gestures] and the belt is laying here. It went like this, and made a sound. That boy, that was driving, quickly screamed, “There is a snake,” he said. “Wait,” I said, “Give it a little more gas.” He pushed the feet, it went good. The snake just fell perfectly in there, where the belt was. Then it went perfectly over the dumpster. And he was pulling the dumpster where the beans fell in. And it fell in there—it was rattling hard. That Mexican came and said, “What are you going to do with it?” I said, “I don’t know. What are you going to do with it?” I told him. He went, got a gun from the pickup. He was running. He killed that snake right there. That bean picker was running, it was idling. I dumped the dumpster. It [the snake] fell on the ground. That Mexican picked it up and put it in the pickup. He took it to the end of the fence he was over there digging. And he buried it. He dug a pretty long hole, he put it in there. It was dangerous to pick beans. Since they started, they would pick some up this long [gestures]. The one that was driving that big truck, was holding a pitchfork. He said, “Get up there and level those beans.” As for me, I don’t think so. ”It’s your truck, you do it,” I told him.

phrases.english_text: My son they got sent to Texas. He used to fight fires—he was a Fire Dancer. He was in that group. When that space shuttle fell, they had to find the remaining parts. They got hired in Texas. He was saying they were seeing snakes, “One right after another we were killing them.” He said “Someone found out we were killing them. Someone came and said ‘The next time I find out one of you all killed a snake, you are going home’.” He said “Sometimes we would be walking over the sage, or something was this tall [gestures]. Sometimes their heads would be above that, doing this [gestures]. They warned us not to kill them.” he said.

phrases.english_text: I did like things like that—working outside. I seen something funny, or it really wasn’t funny. It rained a lot when we were staying in Alabama. They are good to eat, they were telling me.
